evals.name: knowledge-query-routes-to-playbook
evals.prompt: How should I structure a SKILL.md file for a skill with several reference topics?
evals.expected_output: A skill-authoring answer sourced from the playbook content (progressive disclosure: SKILL.md hub + spoke files). The skill serves its distilled body and does NOT run scripts/update.sh or read vendor/SKILL.md.
expectations: Output answers from the skill-authoring playbook content (e.g. hub SKILL.md dispatches, spoke files do the work / progressive disclosure)
The run does NOT run scripts/update.sh or attempt a drift-check / update action (updating is the separate /playbooks:update skill)
The run does NOT read vendor/SKILL.md for this plain knowledge query

evals.name: skill-tool-one-per-call-and-invocation-reach
evals.prompt: When writing a skill that must run both /toolchain:check and /tdd:principles, and that also needs a plugin's :setup skill first, how do Skill-tool calls work?
evals.expected_output: States that the Skill tool takes one skill per call (two skills means two calls). For a disable-model-invocation / user-invoked-only target such as a :setup skill, does not instruct Skill-tool invocation — tells the user to run /plugin:setup instead.
expectations: Output states that the Skill tool takes one skill per call (a step needing two skills is two calls)
Output does NOT instruct invoking a disable-model-invocation / user-invoked-only :setup skill via the Skill tool
Output tells the user (or the authoring guidance says to tell the user) to run the /plugin:setup slash command instead

evals.name: description-caps-and-their-sources
evals.prompt: What length limits apply to a skill description and where does the 1,024 number come from?
evals.expected_output: Names both caps with their sources: 1,024 characters is the Agent Skills specification's validation limit on the description field, enforced on upload paths and not by Claude Code; 1,536 characters is Claude Code's skill-listing truncation of description plus when_to_use (skillListingMaxDescChars), under a listing budget of 1% of the context window that shortens least-invoked skills first. States that when_to_use extends the one description in the listing and that the key use case goes first because truncation is tail-first. Serves reference/authoring-guidance.md rather than restating the page as an instruction.
expectations: Output names 1,024 as the Agent Skills specification validation cap on the description field alone and says Claude Code does not validate it
Output names 1,536 as Claude Code's listing truncation of description plus when_to_use and names the 1% listing budget that shortens least-invoked skills first
Output states that when_to_use extends the single description in the listing and that the key use case goes first
Output does NOT present the 1,024 cap as a Claude Code validation error

evals.name: pre-share-checklist-groups-and-tags
evals.prompt: Give me the checklist to run before publishing a skill.
evals.expected_output: Serves the pre-share checklist from reference/authoring-checklist.md: three groups (core quality, code and scripts, testing), each row tagged mechanical, judgment, or attestation, with mechanical rows naming the skill-quality:check check number that decides them (for example the 500-line cap as check 4 and explicit disable-model-invocation as check 24), and an attestation row for the models the skill was exercised on (haiku, sonnet, opus, fable). Closes by naming /skill-quality:check <skill> as the run that answers the mechanical rows.
expectations: Output presents the three groups: core quality, code and scripts, testing
Output tags rows as mechanical, judgment, or attestation, and mechanical rows name the skill-quality:check check number that decides them
Output includes an attestation row for the models exercised, naming the alias list (haiku, sonnet, opus, fable)
Output names /skill-quality:check <skill> as the closing step and does NOT claim a script verified a judgment or attestation row
